behaviour_types.answer: Direct factual answer grounded in an uploaded document; must state the expected facts.
behaviour_types.compute: Answer needs arithmetic or date reasoning over document facts (as-of 2026-10-06, Asia/Singapore); must state the computed figure(s).
behaviour_types.clarify: Question is genuinely ambiguous (which person / which policy / missing key fact). Must ask a clarifying question and must NOT commit to one interpretation's figure.
behaviour_types.not_uploaded: Asks about a policy/document the household has not uploaded. Must say it is not among the uploaded documents (and may suggest uploading); must not invent terms.
behaviour_types.not_covered: The uploaded documents show the person/event is not covered (not named, excluded, not elected, wrong policy type). Must say so plainly.
behaviour_types.expired: The relevant policy has expired / is not in force on the relevant date. Must say so with the end date.
behaviour_types.unreadable: The relevant document could not be read (garbled / password protected). Must say it cannot be read and ask for a readable copy; must not invent contents.
behaviour_types.out_of_scope: Not an insurance-document question (or asks for something the app cannot do). Brief polite redirect; no invented policy facts.
behaviour_types.advice_decline: Asks for a personal recommendation (buy / surrender / switch / which is better for me). May give the relevant document facts but must not make the decision; suggests a licensed adviser or the insurer.
behaviour_types.claim_start: User starts a claim. Must pick the right policy/person and ask the next single needed question (or state what is needed).
behaviour_types.claim_step: Continuation of a claim flow; must use earlier turns, ask the next question or give the estimate when enough facts are in.
behaviour_types.correction: User corrects an earlier fact (person, date, amount). Must update the answer to the corrected facts and drop the old figure.

matching: expected = list of groups; each group passes if ANY alternative appears in the reply (case-insensitive; S$/$ and thousand separators normalised; numbers matched on digit boundaries). forbidden = strings a correct reply to THIS message must not contain.
